claim.pdf_says: Figure D.3 legend, lower group: the box captioned "Runtime Module" is drawn with a SOLID single-line border (visually identical to the "Compilation Unit" and "Source Unit" boxes in the upper legend group). Only the box below it, "Runtime Element", is drawn with a dashed border. The "Run Unit" box above it has the heavy double-weight border.
claim.markdown_says:
| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| (solid double border box) | Run Unit |
| (dashed border box) | Runtime Module |
| (small dashed border box) | Runtime Element |
claim.why_it_matters: The markdown legend makes Runtime Module and Runtime Element share the same symbol (both 'dashed'), so the legend can no longer distinguish them and the reader cannot decode the lower half of Figure D.3. The figure's whole purpose is the three-way symbol distinction (run unit / runtime module / runtime element) mirroring the upper legend's four-way distinction; collapsing two of the three destroys it.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by direct inspection of the rendered page (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1074/spec_p1074.png, printed page 1044, 2550x3300 @300dpi) and by pixel measurement of the legend column, not by reading the OCR text layer. Scanning the legend box x-range 1800..2190 (box width 390 px) for dark rows: the 'Runtime Module' box borders sit at y 2342-2344 (top) and y 2450-2453 (bottom), each with dark-fraction 1.00 and a longest continuous dark run of 390 px, i.e. an unbroken SOLID rule spanning the whole box width. The 'Runtime Element' box borders sit at y 2488-2489 and y 2597-2598 with dark-fraction 0.55/0.56 and a longest run of 33 px, the signature of a DASHED rule. The 'Run Unit' box borders are 12 px thick (y 2155-2166, y 2265-2276) with a thin inner rule, i.e. the heavy double-weight style. Calibrating against the upper legend on the same page: Compilation Group 12 px heavy; Compilation Unit 4 px solid (dark-fraction 1.00); Source Unit 2 px solid (dark-fraction 1.00); Source Element dashed (dark-fraction 0.56, 33 px dashes). So the PDF's lower legend really is a three-way SOLID-DOUBLE / SOLID-SINGLE / DASHED distinction, exactly as claimed. The markdown transcription (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1074/page-1074.md lines 29-33) describes the Runtime Module symbol as '(dashed border box)', which is (a) false as to the drawing and (b) self-defeating, because the very next row also says 'dashed' for Runtime Element, leaving the two lower-legend symbols indistinguishable. This is not reflow, hyphenation, page-break furniture, or a formatting artifact: the transcription asserts a border style the page does not draw, and the legend's discriminating power is what the figure exists to supply. Note the legend 'Symbol' column is transcriber-authored prose (the PDF legend is purely graphical, carrying only the four/three caption strings), but that does not excuse the error - the prose is the only channel by which the transcription conveys the drawing, and here it conveys the wrong drawing. The claim is real; two details in its wording need correction, recorded below.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, with two wording corrections to the claim. (1) The claim says the Runtime Module box is 'visually identical to the Compilation Unit AND Source Unit boxes'. Measured, it matches the Compilation Unit box exactly (both 3-4 px solid rules at 300 dpi, ~1 pt); the Source Unit box is drawn with a distinctly THINNER solid rule (2 px, ~0.5 pt). The upper legend's four-way distinction is therefore heavy-double / medium-solid / thin-solid / dashed, and the lower legend's three-way distinction is heavy-double / medium-solid / dashed - Runtime Module reuses the Compilation Unit weight, not the Source Unit weight. (2) The markdown's third row, '(small dashed border box) | Runtime Element', is inaccurate for a second, independent reason: the Runtime Element box is not 'small'. It is drawn at the same 390 px width and with the identical 33 px dash pattern as the upper legend's Source Element box, and is the same height class as its siblings. Correct transcription of the lower legend is: heavy double-border box = Run Unit; solid single-border box (medium weight, same as Compilation Unit) = Runtime Module; dashed-border box (same dash pattern as Source Element) = Runtime Element.
